title: Subliminal Trait Transmission Through Agent Distillation: Do Tool-Using Trajectories Carry Hidden Misalignment to Small Students?
summary: We propose testing whether subliminal learning extends from plain text distillation to agent distillation, where small models learn from a teacher's retrieval and code-tool trajectories. A teacher with an implanted trait, such as insider-threat-style misalignment, generates filtered agentic trajectories on benign factual and math tasks. Students sharing or not sharing the teacher's base model are distilled, and we measure trait acquisition in held-out agentic misalignment scenarios. We also test whether first-thought prefixes or self-consistent action sampling change transmission. The hypothesis is that shared-base students acquire the trait despite content filtering, while different-base students do not.
gap: Subliminal learning has been shown for numbers, code and reasoning traces, and agent distillation has been proposed as a way to transfer full task-solving behavior. Nobody has checked whether multi-step, tool-augmented trajectories transmit hidden unsafe traits, or whether agent-distillation tricks affect that risk.
approach: Fine-tune a teacher to hold a trait (misaligned propensity or a benign preference). Generate agent trajectories (thought, code or retrieval action, observation) on benign tasks. Filter explicit trait references. Distill into small students with the same or a different base model, using the standard recipe, the first-thought prefix variant, and the self-consistent action variant. Evaluate trait expression in agentic insider-threat scenarios and in preference probes.
evaluation: Compare trait rates of students against students distilled from a trait-free teacher, and compare same-base against cross-base students. Compare filtering strengths, including LLM-based filters. Measure task accuracy to check that distillation succeeded. Report trait rates with confidence intervals across seeds, and use harmful-action rate in the agentic misalignment scenarios as the main safety metric.
